# Figures (generated by figures/index.py; do not edit)

Run profile: **full** (5,000 Monte Carlo draws; formats pdf, png at 600 dpi). Every figure is drawn by the figures/ package from the data files listed (compute / draw separation).

## Main paper (paper_main/)

### Fig1_floor_area

**Fig1 Floor area: history and projection by demand band** — Floor area built per year, history (census intervals) and the Reference projection 2026-2050, by demand band: positive bands stacked up from zero, negative bands (overbuild absorbed, unconsented additions) down from zero, the net a black line.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig1_floor_area.pdf`, `paper_main/Fig1_floor_area.png`
- Data: `data/baseline/bands_history.csv`, `data/baseline/bands_annual.csv`, `data/baseline/annual.csv`
- This run: Negative bands drawn down from zero: Overbuild absorbed, Unconsented additions, Vacancy, Net replacement (census), Retirement villages (out of scope), Unexplained building; the net (black) is the floor area built. 2026-2050: 85.9 Mm².

### Fig2_reference_carbon

**Fig2 Embodied carbon of the Reference** — Annual embodied carbon of the Reference 2026-2050 by (a) demand band, (b) material and (c) life-cycle stage; materials and stages are never negative.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig2_reference_carbon.pdf`, `paper_main/Fig2_reference_carbon.png`
- Data: `data/baseline/bands_annual.csv`, `data/baseline/annual_by_material.csv`, `data/baseline/annual_by_stage.csv`
- This run: 2026-2050: 20,615 kt CO₂e.

### Fig3_reference_boundaries

**Fig3 The Reference against the planetary boundaries** — (a) Annual carbon, Monte Carlo median with 50% and 90% bands, against the acquired-rights (AR) and ability-to-pay (AtP) boundaries and their zones; (b) cumulative carbon 2026-2050 with the committed range after 2050 as a hollow segment on top, the AR and AtP budgets as ticks, and three thin 100% share bars by demand band, material and stage.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig3_reference_boundaries.pdf`, `paper_main/Fig3_reference_boundaries.png`
- Data: `data/aesa/annual.csv`, `data/montecarlo/annual_REF.csv`, `data/baseline/projection.json`, `data/baseline/bands_annual.csv`, `data/baseline/annual_by_material.csv`, `data/baseline/annual_by_stage.csv`
- This run: Cumulative 2026-2050 20,615 kt (LoE AR 4.63, AtP 18.5); committed after 2050 7,884-8,616 kt. Bands with a negative value are not in the share bar (they reduce the positive stack).

### Fig4_pathways_annual

**Fig4 Pathways against the boundaries** — Annual carbon of the Reference, P1-P5 and TL against AR and AtP: Moderate solid bold, Ambitious the same colour thin dotted.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig4_pathways_annual.pdf`, `paper_main/Fig4_pathways_annual.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/annual.csv`, `data/aesa/annual.csv`
- This run: Cumulative LoE AR: REF 4.63, P5-moderate 3.39, P5-ambitious 2.45, TL 0.98.

### Fig5_waterfall

**Fig5 From the Reference to the theoretical limit** — Cumulative carbon 2026-2050 by demand band along the sequential path Reference -> P1 ... P4 (= P5 Moderate) -> TL1 ... TL9 (= TL); negative bands outlined, hanging from the top of the positive stack; each bar ends at its net total.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig5_waterfall.pdf`, `paper_main/Fig5_waterfall.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/waterfall.csv`
- This run: Moderate: Reference 20,615 kt -> P5 15,073 kt -> TL 4,358 kt; budgets AR 4,451 kt, AtP 1,113 kt. Sequential steps depend on their order (the order-free values are the Shapley values, Fig8).

### Fig6_solution_space

**Fig6 The solution space** — Cumulative level of exceedance of AR and AtP over uniform cuts of 2027-2050 floor area and of carbon per m2 (after Horup et al. 2025), with P1-P5 (Moderate filled, Ambitious hollow) and TL.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig6_solution_space.pdf`, `paper_main/Fig6_solution_space.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/solution_space.csv`, `data/pathways/backcast.json`
- This run: LoE AR = [1,421 + 19,194 (1 - x)(1 - y)] / 4,451 kt; C_2026 = the 2026 cohort's emissions in the window. Lowest LoE AR on the plane (x or y = 100%): 0.32. The AtP line lies outside the plane.

### Fig7_tornado

**Fig7 What moves the Reference** — One-at-a-time ranges of eight inputs, the overbuild absorption timing among them: (a) cumulative carbon 2026-2050, (b) cumulative LoE AR and AtP. Not additive, not a joint interval.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig7_tornado.pdf`, `paper_main/Fig7_tornado.png`
- Data: `data/sensitivity/tornado.csv`
- This run: Reference 20,615 kt (LoE AR 4.63, AtP 18.5); population rows move the budgets with the path; one-at-a-time ranges are not additive.

### Fig8_shapley_levers

**Fig8 What each lever removes** — Shapley values within each combined game (Reference -> P5 Moderate, -> P5 Ambitious, -> TL; exact, 512 subsets) on cumulative carbon 2026-2050: hollow bar Moderate, filled bar Ambitious, large deep-green dot TL; sorted by Ambitious. Standalone effects in ED10.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig8_shapley_levers.pdf`, `paper_main/Fig8_shapley_levers.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/shapley.csv`
- This run: Shapley values within each combined game (Reference -> P5 Moderate, -> P5 Ambitious, -> TL); standalone effects in ED10. Sum over levers (= Reference - P5 / TL, exact): moderate 5,542 kt, ambitious 9,694 kt, tl 16,257 kt; 512 subsets per game.

### D04_household_formation

**Household size vs arrivals; households per consent; new households by source**

- Files: `diagnostics/calibration/D04_household_formation.pdf`, `diagnostics/calibration/D04_household_formation.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D04_household_formation.json`
- This run: Between censuses households are consent-derived, so the relationship in a is partly mechanical (housing supply meets migration). b: households per previous-year consent vary before 2019 and are 0.885–0.889 from 2019: these years are estimated from consents and are not independent evidence. c: history one column per census interval (interval means; households census-anchored at both ends), stacked from population growth and from household-size change; 2024–2025 faint (consent-derived estimates, no census check); projection annual, faded, from 2026; the line is the net of the two parts. A negative part (household-size change, where households grow larger) is drawn as an outlined segment hanging from the top of the stack, so each column ends at its net total (short tick).

### D05_stock_and_vacancy

**Vacancy, stock and dwellings per year by component**

- Files: `diagnostics/calibration/D05_stock_and_vacancy.pdf`, `diagnostics/calibration/D05_stock_and_vacancy.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D05_stock_and_vacancy.json`
- This run: a: The vacancy-rate parameter is held at its published 2023 census value (5.39%; on the consistent definition 2023 is the series maximum, 5.38%, minimum 4.01% in 1996); the 2026 overbuild raises implied stock vacancy temporarily and is absorbed by 2035, so implied vacancy returns to the parameter (5.39% in 2050). c: History: one bar per census interval (interval means; vacancy on one definition, the pooled 2018/2023 empty share, 49.2% of unoccupied dwellings); between censuses annual detail is not identified. Faint bar: 2024–2025, households consent-derived. Projection annual, lighter. History: net replacement is census-measured, the rate of the census dwelling-count identity of each interval (D07; under-construction corrected) x the previous year's stock, the quantity the model uses (2024–2025: the latest rate carried). Projection: demolition replacement, unconsented additions (negative), the recent replacement surge, retirement villages (negative), the 2026 overbuild and the overbuild absorbed (negative payback). Negative parts are outlined, hanging from the top of the positive stack; each bar ends at its net total (tick). Unexplained building (faded red, labelled per interval in thousand dwellings per year): building not explained by household formation, vacancy and census-measured replacement: redevelopment not captured by the census counts, error in the household estimates, or residual; it may be negative.

### D35_overbuild_absorption

**The 2026 overbuild in the Reference: excess, surplus, payback, implied vacancy**

- Files: `diagnostics/calibration/D35_overbuild_absorption.pdf`, `diagnostics/calibration/D35_overbuild_absorption.png`
- Data: `data/baseline/overbuild_absorption_log.csv`
- This run: Reference, median population path (engine.absorb_overbuild). a: the 2026 overbuild, building above the requirement (positive), and the payback paid by building less (negative, outlined, hanging from the top of the overbuild; tick = net); below, the surplus still vacant U and the absorption weight w. The overbuild is absorbed by 2035 along the logistic (w = 1); once absorbed, the remaining 2026 overbuild is paid back in the same year (net 0, the ticks on the zero line). b: the unabsorbed surplus raises implied vacancy temporarily, which returns to the vacancy parameter once it is absorbed. The speed of absorption is bracketed by sensitivity (never absorbed, absorbed by 2030, by 2045).

## Diagnostics: boundaries (diagnostics/boundaries/)

### D18_aesa_sensitivity

**All AESA sensitivity rows: cumulative LoE AR and AtP**

- Files: `diagnostics/boundaries/D18_aesa_sensitivity.pdf`, `diagnostics/boundaries/D18_aesa_sensitivity.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D18_aesa_sensitivity.json`
- This run: One setting changed per row; labels show the cumulative LoE of that row and its change from the Reference. Rows that do not enter a principle (e.g. the GDP measure for AR) show no change. Percentages are relative to carbon 2026–2050 (time-resolved accounting); fixed absolute terms such as soil carbon loss therefore show larger percentage effects than under whole-life accounting. The largest effects on the AR and AtP LoE, grouped: Extended Data ED4 (carbon: ED1).

### D21_fan_and_boundaries

**Monte Carlo fan of carbon, the AR base window and the boundary bands**

- Files: `diagnostics/boundaries/D21_fan_and_boundaries.pdf`, `diagnostics/boundaries/D21_fan_and_boundaries.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D21_fan_and_boundaries.json`
- This run: Reference. AR base window 2016–2025 at 2025 factors, soil only on non-replacement floor area (as the projection); the thin history line is joined to the 2026 Monte Carlo median. Boundary bands: AR varies with the NZ population of each draw and its AR base (recomputed from the draw's 2025 carbon factors), AtP with population only; AR 5th–95th within 9.9% of the median in every year.

### D22_boundaries

**Boundaries AR and AtP 2025-2050, population modifier, components**

- Files: `diagnostics/boundaries/D22_boundaries.pdf`, `diagnostics/boundaries/D22_boundaries.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D22_boundaries.json`
- This run: 2 °C carrying capacity (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015). Log axis: the AtP boundary is 25.0% of the AR boundary in every year: both scale with P_NZ(t) / P_W(t) (static design), so their ratio is constant.

### D23_annual_loe

**Annual level of exceedance by variant with Monte Carlo bands**

- Files: `diagnostics/boundaries/D23_annual_loe.pdf`, `diagnostics/boundaries/D23_annual_loe.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D23_annual_loe.json`
- This run: 2 °C carrying capacity (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015). Log axis: the AtP LoE is 4.0 × the AR LoE in every year. Monte Carlo bands: within-variant uncertainty (population, dwelling size, completion rate, carbon factors). Carbon: construction (A1–A5 and soil) plus maintenance (B2, B4) occurring each year, buildings built from 2026; later events and C1–C4 are committed after 2050; A1–A3 of the case-study items decarbonised after Horup et al. 2025 (item-level mapping), A4–A5 e^(−0.01 (t − 2025)) after Resch et al. 2021, C1–C4 and soil at 2025.

### D24_headroom

**Intensity, floor area and carbon per dwelling that would fit each boundary**

- Files: `diagnostics/boundaries/D24_headroom.pdf`, `diagnostics/boundaries/D24_headroom.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D24_headroom.json`
- This run: Reference, median population. Fitting carbon per m² = B(t) / floor area(t); fitting floor area = B(t) / (carbon per m² of the Reference); per dwelling = B(t) / dwellings built(t), dwellings = floor area / blended dwelling size. Carbon: construction (A1–A5 and soil) plus maintenance (B2, B4) occurring each year, buildings built from 2026; later events and C1–C4 are committed after 2050; A1–A3 of the case-study items decarbonised after Horup et al. 2025 (item-level mapping), A4–A5 e^(−0.01 (t − 2025)) after Resch et al. 2021, C1–C4 and soil at 2025; carbon per m² also varies with the mix and the soil-bearing share. 2 °C carrying capacity (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015).

- Data: `data/figure_source/D27_variants_vs_boundaries.json`
- This run: The boundaries are the same in every variant (same population path). Boundaries: 2 °C carrying capacity (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015), SOS 6.81e+12 and I_glob 5.58e+13 kg CO₂e per year; AR: Horup et al. 2025 Eq. 1 (base 2016–2025); AtP: Hjalsted et al. 2021 Eqs. 5–6 (GDP per capita, PPP, 2024); AtP is 25.0% of AR in every year (static design). Carbon: construction (A1–A5 and soil) plus maintenance (B2, B4) occurring each year, buildings built from 2026; later events and C1–C4 are committed after 2050; A1–A3 of the case-study items decarbonised after Horup et al. 2025 (item-level mapping), A4–A5 e^(−0.01 (t − 2025)) after Resch et al. 2021, C1–C4 and soil at 2025.
